From: Alex Park <alex@brightlane.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Repeated streaming disconnects during long inference sessions

Hey Karthik,

We're seeing intermittent disconnects when using Redwood's streaming endpoint in our production canary. It happens roughly every 10-12 minutes during long generative sessions (>6k tokens). The client logs show a gRPC stream closed with UNAVAILABLE and no clear error code from your side. We captured a session dump and repro steps (attached).

Quick facts:
- App: BrightLane editor (web) on Chrome 114
- SDK: official JS SDK v2.1.0 (streaming)
- Region: us-west1
- Approx impact: ~3% of streaming sessions over the past 24h
- Temporary workaround: reconnect and resume with last token, but UX hit is significant

Can you confirm if this is likely a client-side keepalive/idle issue vs server-side eviction? Also, we had previously asked for a way to pass a customer tenant id for better attribution (we're multitenant inside BrightLane). Is there any recommended request header or SDK field to propagate a BrightLane tenant id so we can correlate across our logs and yours?

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Platform Engineer
BrightLane

- brightlane-session_dump.log (text)
- repro_steps.txt (text)

Thanks for the ping and the dump — quick read: this looks like the termination is coming from the fronting layer (our edge reverse-proxy) closing idle streams after ~10 minutes when no traffic is observed at the transport layer. Two likely contributors: (1) browser-level TCP keepalives are infrequent, and (2) current SDK doesn't surface a per-stream keepalive ping by default.

Short-term mitigation (field playbook):
- Recommend customers bump the client keepalive interval in the SDK to 30s for streaming sessions (JS SDK: StreamingClient.keepaliveIntervalMs = 30000). We'll add this to the KB article.
- Advise implementing resumable sessions on reconnect using a client-side resume token (we can supply guidance).
- Server-side: we can add a 15s grace window in the edge for select accounts (config flag) as an emergency rollover; needs Platform ops enablement but no code change.

Longer-term product/runtime changes I propose:
1) Add a first-class SDK field/header to propagate tenant context: header name proposal \"X-Redwood-Tenant\" (or metadata key for gRPC). This allows edge logs and runtime traces to correlate BrightLane tenant ids with session ids. Implementation scope: SDK (client-side header), edge (log parsing), runtime tracing. Backward compatibility: if header absent, no change in behavior.
2) Add an idempotency/resume token field for streaming sessions (e.g., X-Redwood-ResumeId) to allow client to resume cleanly after disconnects.

I can prototype the runtime parsing for X-Redwood-Tenant and the keepalive guidance today. If Product signs off on header name and privacy considerations we can schedule an SDK patch in the next minor release.

Logan
Platform Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

This matches a product request we've seen from other customers (tenant propagation + resume semantics). A few product asks / constraints before we make the SDK change:

1) Header name and semantics: prefer \"X-Redwood-Tenant\" but insist that it is only used for telemetry/tracing/attribution — it must not alter routing or access decisions unless the account explicitly enables tenant routing (security concern).
2) Privacy/compliance: require we document PII guidance — tenant ids should be non-PII stable ids. For Private deployments we need guidance for customers who run their own control plane (we can't inject headers there).
3) Backward compatibility: SDK must support both the new header and a deprecated metadata slot for 6 months; runtime should never reject requests without the header.
4) Rollout: request a canary (Logging + Trace correlation) for BrightLane account only, then a small percent canary, then full release. If Platform needs an exception to rollout order (e.g., enable edge grace for BrightLane immediately), I'm okay approving that as a one-off SLA mitigation.

Please prepare a short spec covering header name, sample SDK snippet for JS/Go/python, and acceptance criteria (logs/traces show tenant id present and no routing change). Once I sign off we can communicate timeline to BrightLane.

Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the details and the dump. Internal summary and next steps below; copying our runtime and product leads so you have a single point of contact.

Summary:
- Likely cause: edge idle close after ~10m; client keepalive frequency is a contributing factor.
- Short-term mitigation we recommend now: increase SDK keepalive to 30s and implement client resume token. Our KB will include sample code.
- Product-approved plan: we will add an SDK header \"X-Redwood-Tenant\" for tenant attribution (read-only for tracing/logging). Marissa is approving a BrightLane-only canary and a limited edge grace toggle as an SLA mitigation if needed.

Action items & owners:
- Logan: prototype runtime header parsing + enable BrightLane-edge-grace flag (Platform ops) for immediate mitigation. Target: today for ops toggle, prototyping by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: signoff on header spec and publish acceptance criteria. Target: 48 hours.
- Soojin: coordinate commercial acknowledgement and customer communication; confirm if BrightLane needs an SLA note.
- Karthik: I will share example SDK snippet and the KB playbook once Logan confirms the keepalive guidance.

We will run a short sync tomorrow 10:30am PT to align on the canary steps. If BrightLane is available for a short test after the flag is enabled that would help validate.
